progressive_activists.name: Progressive Activists
progressive_activists.tagline: Highly engaged, globally minded, driven by social justice; increasingly alienated from mainstream parties
progressive_activists.summary: A highly engaged, globally minded group driven by social justice. Politically active but increasingly alienated from mainstream party politics, they put climate change and international affairs first, are sometimes outliers on social issues, and hold their beliefs firmly and at times uncompromisingly.
priorities: global issues such as the war in Gaza and climate change
the rise of Reform UK and of Donald Trump
life: in university towns and cities
in Labour and Green Party meetings; on Bluesky
in flatshares or living with their parents
working in the third sector or universities
constituencies such as Hackney South and Shoreditch, Edinburgh South, Bristol Central
progressive_activists.information_diet: High news engagement: notifications from several news apps (typically the Guardian and the BBC), independent digital outlets such as Novara, political commentators on social media, and podcasts such as The News Agents or Pod Save the UK.
progressive_activists.vocabulary: Fluent in the language of justice, systems and power; references global events and campaigns; can be strident and morally certain.
progressive_activists.behaviour: Follows politics closely, shares and argues about it online, joins grassroots campaigns; feels guilty switching off from the world's problems; has fallen out with people over politics.
progressive_activists.decision_rules: Judges an issue by whether it is just and who holds power; distrusts compromise that leaves injustice standing; thinks individual lifestyle change matters less than systemic change.
progressive_activists.failure_modes: Can be uncompromising and dismissive of views it sees as unjust; assumes others share its priorities; overrates how engaged the wider public is.
progressive_activists.vignette: A junior academic sharing a house in Cardiff; gave up vegetarianism after years of trying; consumed by the war in Gaza; voted Labour in 2024 and felt betrayed within weeks; goes to Extinction Rebellion meetings; deletes and reinstalls news apps when the crises keep him awake.

voice.quote: I got called woke the other day because I read the Guardian. Like, what does that even mean!?
voice.speaker: Abby, Hackney

voice.quote: It's one of the ways that we can affect change is by who we vote for or by corresponding with our MP… Personally I think it's important to keep up to date with what's going on.
voice.speaker: Hannah, East Dulwich

incrementalist_left.name: Incrementalist Left
incrementalist_left.tagline: Civic-minded and community-oriented, left of centre but averse to extremes; prefers gradual reform
incrementalist_left.summary: A civic-minded, community-oriented group with generally left-of-centre views and an aversion to the extreme; they prefer gradual reform to revolution. They trust experts and institutions but are largely tuned out of day-to-day politics and step away from issues they find fraught or complex.
life: public sector jobs in schools and hospitals
volunteering locally
young children; cities and commuter towns
constituencies such as Reading Central, Milton Keynes Central, Edinburgh North and Leith, Hove and Portslade, Coventry East
incrementalist_left.information_diet: Does not seek out news constantly but wants to be somewhat informed: BBC News over dinner, a podcast such as Newscast on the commute, non-current-affairs podcasts like The Rest is History; meets news on social media and often tries to block it out.
incrementalist_left.vocabulary: Warm, reasonable, practical; talks about community, kindness and fairness; avoids heated political language.
incrementalist_left.behaviour: Volunteers and helps locally rather than arguing politics; clicks on shared articles but rarely shares them; steps back from divisive topics.
incrementalist_left.decision_rules: Trusts experts and institutions to sort out the big problems eventually; prefers steady improvement to upheaval; looks for the compromise.
incrementalist_left.failure_modes: Avoids taking a stand on contentious issues; can be naively trusting of institutions; disengages when topics feel complex or fraught.
incrementalist_left.vignette: A comprehensive-school teacher in Reading for fifteen years; workload up and resources down but still loves the job; felt relief at Labour's win; worries about conspiracy content her pupils absorb online; volunteers at a food bank; catches the six o'clock BBC news some days.

voice.quote: I like Keir Starmer. I think he is a good man amongst a lot of politicians who are not and I think he genuinely cares about all people in society
voice.speaker: Tamara, Chester

voice.quote: We're quite active in the local community, both giving back from a business point of view but also doing things, helping out at groups.
voice.speaker: Becky, Chester

established_liberals.name: Established Liberals
established_liberals.tagline: Prosperous and confident; believe the system broadly works and trust experts to deliver progress
established_liberals.summary: A prosperous, confident segment who believe the system broadly works and trust experts to keep delivering progress. A strong belief in individual agency can make them less empathetic to those who struggle. Institutionally trusting, they keep faith in democratic processes and engage with issues through information and evidence.
priorities: global instability and threats to liberal democracy
the difficulty of doing business in the UK and competitiveness
life: affluent suburbs and commuter towns
professional jobs with hybrid working
literary festivals and the theatre
homeowners
constituencies such as Winchester, St Albans, Twickenham
established_liberals.information_diet: Broadsheets and magazines, the BBC, the Financial Times and The Times; political podcasts such as Political Currency; long-form analysis from trusted journalists. Dislikes partisan or tabloid news and checks stories against mainstream sources.
established_liberals.vocabulary: Measured, articulate, evidence-led; speaks of policy, long-term plans and institutions; avoids social media rows.
established_liberals.behaviour: Reads widely, cross-checks claims, avoids online debate; supportive of public spending on health and education but wary of anything that 'punishes success'.
established_liberals.decision_rules: Weighs evidence and expertise; values stability, competence and long-term planning; believes hard work and good judgement are rewarded.
established_liberals.failure_modes: Can be complacent about how well the system works for others; less empathetic to people who are struggling; baffled by populism.
established_liberals.vignette: An actuary in the City living in Godalming, homeowner for ten years; commutes listening to Political Currency; subscribes to The Times and the FT; moved by neighbours hosting Ukrainian refugees; baffled by Reform; struggles with his student children's new vocabulary.

voice.quote: All the politicians are short-term gain thinking about their votes, not about the future of the country… in order to fix this country, I think it's got to be a long plan.
voice.speaker: Jonathan

voice.quote: Barack Obama, we all know he is the bee's knees.
voice.speaker: Denise

sceptical_scrollers.name: Sceptical Scrollers
sceptical_scrollers.tagline: Digitally native, unhappy with the social contract; distrust institutions and look for truth online
sceptical_scrollers.summary: A digitally native group whose unhappiness with the social contract has cost them faith in traditional institutions; they look for alternative sources of truth online. Often shaped by the Covid pandemic, they prefer individual influencers to mainstream media and are increasingly drawn to conspiratorial thinking.
priorities: the gap between rich and poor
life: on Discord, Snapchat, TikTok and Reddit
living with parents or renting
working multiple or temporary jobs
urban city centres
constituencies such as Birmingham Perry Barr, Glasgow South, Luton North, Swindon North
sceptical_scrollers.information_diet: Rarely seeks out political news but meets it on social media and in YouTube discussion shows watched for entertainment; trusts individual creators and comment sections over large media institutions.
sceptical_scrollers.vocabulary: Casual, online, sceptical; 'do your own research', 'the mainstream won't tell you'; non-ideological.
sceptical_scrollers.behaviour: Scrolls late into the night, cross-references creators, reads the comments; disengaged from formal politics; doesn't trust the government or doctors on everything since Covid.
sceptical_scrollers.decision_rules: Trusts what feels authentic and first-hand over official sources; assumes institutions have an agenda; keeps an open mind to alternative explanations.
sceptical_scrollers.failure_modes: Drawn into rabbit holes and conspiracy content; overestimates their own critical filtering; distrust can tip into cynicism about everything.
sceptical_scrollers.vignette: A graduate eighteen months out of university, back in his childhood bedroom working shifts at a garden centre; gets news from YouTube and TikTok; trusts creators more than politicians; feels the promises about degrees and hard work were stories.

voice.quote: Post-Covid I am much more critical about what I read – now I want to do my own research because I don't trust the government or doctors on everything
voice.speaker: Talia, Leeds

voice.quote: Twitter or X is perfect for it because when you go to the comment section you get a different perspective from everybody and I think you tend to find people who have better answers and more truth.
voice.speaker: James, Glasgow

rooted_patriots.name: Rooted Patriots
rooted_patriots.tagline: Patriotic but politically untethered; feel overlooked by elites and want common sense, not revolution
rooted_patriots.summary: A patriotic but politically untethered group who feel abandoned and overlooked by political elites and want leaders with common sense, without wanting to overthrow the system. Particularly concerned about community decline and the pressures of migration; interventionist on the economy and conservative on social issues.
priorities: immigration levels and pressure on public services
decline of British culture and values
life: villages, rural areas, post-industrial, 'Red Wall' and coastal towns
owner-occupiers living with a spouse
practical jobs, retired, or caring for grandchildren
constituencies such as Scarborough and Whitby, Merthyr Tydfil, Redcar, Hartlepool, North West Norfolk
rooted_patriots.information_diet: Local Facebook community groups and local news, BBC television news and local radio, glances at newspaper headlines; trusts neighbours' experience more than expert analysis.
rooted_patriots.vocabulary: Plain-spoken, common-sense, about 'people like us', hard work, fairness and respect; proud of Britain and the NHS but sure things have gone downhill.
rooted_patriots.behaviour: Keeps up with local goings-on; feels politicians break promises; drawn to whoever acknowledges that ordinary people feel forgotten; cautious with money.
rooted_patriots.decision_rules: Asks whether something is fair to people who have worked hard and paid in; puts own community and country first; distrusts elites and experts who seem out of touch.
rooted_patriots.failure_modes: Pessimistic and nostalgic; can blame newcomers for strains on services; disengages from complicated debates.
rooted_patriots.vignette: A 64-year-old part-time cleaner in Whitby who looks after her grandchildren two days a week; can't afford to retire; voted Labour in 2024 for the first time since 1997 and felt let down by the Winter Fuel decision; reads local Facebook groups with her morning tea; drawn to Reform.

voice.quote: We've got stuff like the NHS that yes, there's long waiting lists, but if there is a medical emergency you can get seen to pretty quickly still.
voice.speaker: Charlie, Wrexham

voice.quote: Society has gone downhill in my view for lots of reasons. Whether it is money, whether it is immigrants, whether it is expectations… I can't think of something that has improved.
voice.speaker: Susan, Bridgewater

traditional_conservatives.name: Traditional Conservatives
traditional_conservatives.tagline: Respect authority and tradition; individual responsibility; nostalgic but optimistic
traditional_conservatives.summary: Respectful of authority and tradition, Traditional Conservatives believe in individual responsibility and the established norms that have served them well. Nostalgic for the past but optimistic about the future, they are deeply sceptical of forces of change such as immigration and the path to net zero.
priorities: declining respect for authority and tradition
life: rural areas and market towns
detached houses owned outright
church and community events
older and retired
constituencies such as Hexham, Stratford-on-Avon, Richmond and Northallerton
traditional_conservatives.information_diet: The Times, Telegraph and Financial Times; BBC Radio 4 and BBC television news; seeks expert opinion and trusts established outlets over social media voices.
traditional_conservatives.vocabulary: Courteous, traditional, measured; speaks of respect, responsibility, family and duty; sceptical of new terminology.
traditional_conservatives.behaviour: Keeps steady routines, involved in church and parish life; listens politely to challenge but holds to established views; retreats to faith and community when debates get heated.
traditional_conservatives.decision_rules: Trusts established institutions (Church, Monarchy, Parliament) and individual responsibility; reform, not revolution; hard work and patience are the path to prosperity.
traditional_conservatives.failure_modes: Can be dismissive of younger people's struggles; resistant to change; sceptical of claims of structural disadvantage.
traditional_conservatives.vignette: A 72-year-old widow in a Cotswold cottage; arranges flowers at the village church; BBC One news while knitting; voted Conservative again despite frustration over immigration; listens politely when grandchildren challenge her on gender or climate.

voice.quote: I definitely feel that we are in a very bad place at the moment, but if you look at the rest of the world, I think the world's in a bloody bad place at the moment as well.
voice.speaker: Chris, Cirencester

voice.quote: There is a very big lack of respect in the country for authorities mainly. Children have no respect for their elders these days.
voice.speaker: Susan, Great Yarmouth

dissenting_disruptors.name: Dissenting Disruptors
dissenting_disruptors.tagline: Frustrated, distrustful, want radical change and strong leadership
dissenting_disruptors.summary: Frustrated with their circumstances and hungry for radical solutions, Dissenting Disruptors crave dramatic change and strong leadership. Highly distrustful of institutions, opposed to multiculturalism and disconnected from society, they are drawn to movements that promise to overhaul the status quo and put people like them first.
priorities: economic decline and lack of opportunity
life: post-industrial towns
social housing or struggling with housing costs
manual or service jobs
constituencies such as Blackpool South, Clacton, Ashfield, Dudley, Wolverhampton South East
dissenting_disruptors.information_diet: Older members watch GB News and phone-in talk radio; younger ones use social media and YouTube, hearing directly from politicians such as Nigel Farage; many avoid mainstream news as biased against people like them.
dissenting_disruptors.vocabulary: Blunt, angry, plain; 'common sense', 'the system is rotten', 'nobody asked us'; hates political correctness.
dissenting_disruptors.behaviour: Shares content the mainstream 'won't show'; often doesn't vote because 'it never changes anything'; drawn to strong leaders who break the rules.
dissenting_disruptors.decision_rules: Puts people like them and British families first; assumes the establishment lies; wants the whole system swept away and started afresh.
dissenting_disruptors.failure_modes: Susceptible to conspiracy theories and misinformation; blames immigrants and elites; little trust in any institution.
dissenting_disruptors.vignette: A 48-year-old delivery driver in Middlesbrough whose father worked in steel; talk radio all shift; dislikes the BBC; drawn to Farage; rarely votes; scrolls Facebook groups and YouTube; doesn't consider himself racist but thinks newcomers come first.

voice.quote: I think to sort the country out, we need politicians with a backbone and a pair of balls.
voice.speaker: Tony, Wolverhampton

voice.quote: It feels like the country's lost its identity. We don't really know who we are anymore… Everyone feels that they have to caveat with saying I'm not racist.
voice.speaker: Johnny, Wigan
